title: Recipe 29 — Permissions Deep Dive (ask the engine, don't read the table)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Five rule sources, four modes, one glob grammar — and one security-critical invariant we are going to try to break.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — only the last two beats need it.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the authoring layer — worked example 1

beats.label: Type the plainest agent
beats.cue: “Layer 3 is the spec, and the spec is where you should author. Start with an agent that has no rules at all.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's coding-agent posture
beats.cue: “Read free, writes scoped to src, bun and git allow-listed, everything else Bash asks, rm -rf denied. Ten rules — and note which one is written first.”

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Clean. Note what lint does not do: it never decides a single tool call — it only checks the rules parse.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The rules survive lowering verbatim, in the order you wrote them. Hold that thought — the order IS the policy.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli, permissions block included

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, boots it: GREEN. It also installs the permission engine we're about to interrogate.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate. Also lands live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/permission-engine, which the decision beats import.

beats.label: Find the two gates in the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Ten rules went in tagged source: yaml, and the builtin layer sits under them. This is the whole RuleSet the engine sees.”

verify.note: 3 lines — the alwaysAsk Bash(**), the alwaysDeny Bash(rm -rf *), and the builtin layer import

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Read the permissionRules object: five named layers, and yours is the yaml one.”

groups.title: Beat 3 · ask the engine, don't read the table

beats.label: Decide seven real tool calls
beats.cue: “Same engine the runtime uses, same rules we just typed. Read is free, bun and git status are free, a write inside src is free — and `rm -rf node_modules` comes back ASK, not deny. Look at the rule order: the recipe declares the catch-all `alwaysAsk Bash(**)` ABOVE `alwaysDeny Bash(rm -rf *)`, and within a layer the FIRST matching rule wins. There is no deny-beats-ask tier — so that deny never fires. This is the footgun, in a committed example.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const y=Bun.YAML.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("live/crewhaus.yaml","utf8")); const {evaluate}=await import("./live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/permission-engine/dist/index.js"); const rs={flag:[],settings:[],yaml:y.permissions.rules.map(r=>({...r,source:"yaml"})),hooks:[],builtin:[]}; const want={"Read x.ts":"allow","Bash bun test":"allow","Bash git status":"allow","Bash curl example.com":"ask","Bash rm -rf node_modules":"ask","Write src/a.ts":"allow","Write docs/a.md":"ask"}; const t=(n,i,ro,de)=>({toolName:n,input:i,readOnly:ro,destructive:de}); const calls=[["Read x.ts",t("Read",{file_path:"x.ts"},true,false)],["Bash bun test",t("Bash",{command:"bun test"},false,true)],["Bash git status",t("Bash",{command:"git status"},false,true)],["Bash curl example.com",t("Bash",{command:"curl example.com"},false,true)],["Bash rm -rf node_modules",t("Bash",{command:"rm -rf node_modules"},false,true)],["Write src/a.ts",t("Write",{file_path:"src/a.ts"},false,true)],["Write docs/a.md",t("Write",{file_path:"docs/a.md"},false,true)]]; for(const [k,c] of calls){const got=evaluate(c,y.permissions.mode,rs); console.log(k.padEnd(26)+" -> "+got); if(got!==want[k]) throw new Error(k+": got "+got+", want "+want[k]);}'

verify.note: asserts all seven decisions against crewhaus 0.4.2's engine. The engine walks source layers in priority order and takes the FIRST matching rule inside a layer — there is no tier-first deny > ask > allow. Recipe 29's worked example puts `alwaysDeny Bash(rm -rf *)` BELOW the catch-all `alwaysAsk Bash(**)`, so it is shadowed and `rm -rf node_modules` resolves to ask. Move the deny above the catch-all and this beat fails with deny.

beats.label: Hold the pattern grammar to its table
beats.cue: “Nine rows straight out of the recipe's grammar table. The one to remember: a single star does not cross a slash, so Bash(rm -rf *) never matches rm -rf slash.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const {compilePattern,matchesPattern}=await import("./live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/tool-permission-matcher/dist/index.js"); const m=(p,t,i)=>matchesPattern(compilePattern(p),t,i); const rows=[["Read","Read",{file_path:"anything"},true],["Bash(git *)","Bash",{command:"git status"},true],["Bash(git *)","Bash",{command:"npm i"},false],["Write(**/src/**)","Write",{file_path:"pkg/src/a.ts"},true],["Write(**/src/**)","Write",{file_path:"docs/a.md"},false],["Bash(rm -rf *)","Bash",{command:"rm -rf tmp"},true],["Bash(rm -rf *)","Bash",{command:"rm -rf /"},false],["Bash(**)","Bash",{command:"rm -rf /"},true],["*__list_directory","fs__list_directory",{},true]]; for(const [p,tool,i,want] of rows){const got=m(p,tool,i); console.log(p.padEnd(18)+" vs "+tool+" "+JSON.stringify(i)+" -> "+got); if(got!==want) throw new Error(p+" vs "+tool+": got "+got);}'

verify.note: all nine rows of the recipe's pattern-grammar table hold, including `*` not crossing `/` and the MCP-namespace `*__list_directory` row

groups.title: Beat 4 · the bypass guard — try to break it

beats.label: Type the same agent again
beats.cue: “Second scratch spec. Identical agent — one extra line is all it takes to try to switch the guard off.”

beats.label: Ask for bypass in the spec
beats.cue: “The escape hatch, declared in a file — exactly what a malicious or careless commit would do.”

beats.label: Watch the parser refuse it
beats.cue: “Deliberate rejection, exit 1: bypass is rejected from a spec file, and the message names the only legal source.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `✗ [parse] <spec>: permissions.mode: bypass is rejected — bypass mode is only available via the --permission-mode CLI flag, never from a spec file`; lint: 1 error(s)

beats.label: Use the one legal source
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same mode, typed by a human at the shell. That's the whole difference — and it's the difference that matters.”

verify.note: interactive REPL in bypass mode; needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.

groups.title: One more thing · plan mode, and the sandbox floor under it

beats.label: Type the read-only investigator
beats.cue: “The recipe's fourth worked example is two lines long, and it is the strictest posture there is.”

beats.label: Set mode: plan
beats.cue: “No rules at all. Plan mode is not a rule set — it is a blanket answer: reads yes, writes no.”

beats.label: Prove the two floors hold
beats.cue: “Plan mode denies the write with zero rules configured — and separately, a tool that declares requiresSandbox is denied outright when no sandbox is wired. Fail-closed, both times.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const y=Bun.YAML.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("live/plan.yaml","utf8")); const {evaluateWithReason}=await import("./live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/permission-engine/dist/index.js"); const e={flag:[],settings:[],yaml:[],hooks:[],builtin:[]}; const m=y.permissions.mode; const d=(n,f,mo)=>evaluateWithReason({toolName:n,input:{},...f},mo||m,e); const r=d("Read",{readOnly:true,destructive:false}); const w=d("Write",{readOnly:false,destructive:true}); if(r.decision!=="allow"||w.decision!=="deny") throw new Error("plan mode did not deny the write"); console.log(m+" mode: Read -> allow, Write -> deny"); const p=d("Python",{readOnly:false,destructive:true,requiresSandbox:true},"default"); if(p.decision!=="deny") throw new Error("the sandbox floor did not hold"); console.log("default mode: Python -> deny — "+p.reason)'

verify.note: plan mode: Read -> allow, Write -> deny; default mode: Python -> deny with the requiresSandbox reason (recipe 30 is what wires the sandbox that lifts it)
